approval_required_for: Any architecture or pipeline-topology change beyond the checker-backed operator_stream_pipeline, including decoder operator order, stage insertion/removal, residual skip sources, branch/join fire rules, or MLP split/join topology.

Any change to model or shape facts including GQA head counts, group size, RoPE policy, causal mask policy, seq_len_bound, hidden size, intermediate size, stream lane count, transfer order, or transfer-unit policy.
Any numeric precision, rounding, saturation, accumulator, tolerance, or golden-output change.
Any trusted-template replacement, major template-library/template-metadata change, or free-form RTL generation outside the approved template library.

Any concrete DDR base-address assignment or memory-layout/AXI/DDR address-map change, including AXI data width, address width, WSTRB width, 64-byte alignment, XDMA device index, control/status apertures, raw register/DDR runtime protocol, activation ping/pong policy, or double-buffered weight policy.
Any ambiguous backend/app-shell target selection without cited board materials and real Vivado/tool evidence.
Any attempt to treat symbolic_first_order latency or static pipeline-planning evidence as timing, throughput, RTL correctness, or hardware-pass evidence.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block transition to parameter_binding. Keep the candidate pipeline plan and team action queue behind a stage_artifact_trust_barrier, localize the failing SACG/action-audit field, and do not consume unpromoted artifacts downstream. If the failure invalidates the checked Stage 3 contract rather than action metadata, open a stage_backtrack_request or stop because the pipeline_planning retry budget is already at 2 attempts.
executable_actions.rationale: The current stage passed with 10/10 checks, command return code 0, and no open SACG retry, backtrack, or contamination blockers. Promote only the checker-backed pipeline contract and normalized handoff lineage before any downstream consumption.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block code_generation and later stages. Localize the mismatch to the affected stage, edge, template parameter, numeric field, boundary contract, or memory/stream handoff. Repair only within approved parameter-binding bounds and rerun the same checkers; any topology, numeric-policy, memory-layout, AXI, or template-library change requires approval and likely backtrack to pipeline_planning.
executable_actions.rationale: The next bounded stage is parameter_binding. It must materialize the promoted Stage 3 operator, stream, numeric, template, and memory-runtime handoff facts without changing the checked pipeline semantics.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep code_generation blocked and quarantine unpromoted Stage 4 artifacts. If the repair cannot stay within template-parameter, boundary-contract, numeric-policy, and memory-runtime handoff bounds, emit a stage_backtrack_request to pipeline_planning and require explicit approval for the implicated architecture, numeric, template, or memory change.
executable_actions.rationale: If the next stage fails, the repair loop must be bounded and checker-driven: tool output first, then contract-guided localization, then targeted parameter or manifest repair, then rerun of the failed checker set. It must not mutate golden outputs, loosen tolerance, or bypass the promoted Stage 3 contract.

stage_passed is true on attempt 2 of the bounded 2 attempts. Because the stage passed, no same-stage retry is needed; if a new Stage 3 semantic failure is discovered, retry budget exhaustion must be handled by bounded metadata repair, backtrack, or stop rather than an unbounded retry.
SACG memory explicitly reports no active_contamination_barriers, no open_retry_requests, and no open_backtrack_requests. There is no SACG blocker preventing downstream progress.

No retry_reconciliation_contract is supplied, so there are no previous failed same-stage artifacts to distinguish from candidate retry artifacts for this decision. The promoted contract should still exclude unpromoted draft or duplicate team-action artifacts.

The accepted candidate is a 9-stage decoder operator_stream_pipeline with 13 data edges and 13 mirrored stream edges, preserving the supplied RMSNorm, self-attention, residual, gated MLP, and output order.

Per the supplied stage-gate interpretation, current-stage blockers are clear: the Stage 3 static planning checks passed. Concrete DDR address assignment, runtime ABI materialization, code generation, real simulator evidence, Vivado evidence, and board runtime evidence are later-stage obligations, not current-stage blockers.

The memory/runtime information is a Stage 3 handoff contract only: six required regions, activation ping/pong, double-buffered weights, 512-bit DDR AXI facts, 64-byte alignment policy, and XDMA runtime requirements are preserved, but exact aligned base addresses must not be guessed in Stage 3.

Static liveness, stream, and symbolic_first_order latency evidence do not constitute hardware correctness, timing closure, throughput, or board pass evidence. Later verification must follow the leaf/operator, connected single-transformer-layer, then board-accurate AXI/DDR wrapped-system repair loop.

The design-team aggregate is broad and contains overlapping later-stage handoff actions, but the latest architect result and action-normalization record provide a bounded path: promote the checked Stage 3 contract, then enter parameter_binding with a normalized handoff queue.
proposed_actions: Proceed to parameter_binding; do not retry pipeline_planning, backtrack, or stop on the supplied evidence.
Promote only the checked pipeline_planning SACG state and record a trust manifest so unpromoted draft actions or duplicate handoff artifacts are not consumed as validated downstream inputs.
Run parameter_binding static/template/numeric/boundary/stream/memory checks from the promoted Stage 3 contract before any code_generation consumption.

If parameter_binding fails, use tool-output-driven localization and bounded repair, then rerun the failed checker set; require approval and/or backtrack for any architecture, numeric, template-library, or memory-layout change.

Keep code_generation, concrete DDR address assignment, runtime ABI, real simulator evidence, Vivado/backend, and board runtime blocked until their respective later-stage checker gates provide evidence.
risks: Action-queue contamination risk: the team aggregate includes overlapping Stage 4/5/6 handoff actions, so downstream tools must consume one normalized promoted contract lineage rather than multiple draft artifact names.

Parameter-binding drift risk: Stage 4 could accidentally alter operator order, residual skip sources, GQA/RoPE fields, stream/data edge order, numeric widths, accumulator policy, or trusted-template boundaries.

Data-order and transfer-count risk: token/tile/lane/word ordering and full-beat transfer counts must remain identical across parameter binding, code generation manifests, weight packing, runtime commands, and verification manifests.

Memory/runtime risk: concrete DDR regions, activation ping/pong buffers, double-buffered weights, 512-bit AXI data width, 37-bit address width, WSTRB width, 64-byte alignment, XDMA device index, and raw register/DDR protocol remain later-stage obligations and require approval if changed.

Numeric/golden risk: fp16 activation/weight paths, fp32 accumulation where specified, nearest_even rounding, saturation=false, and golden-reference tolerances must be preserved; modifying golden outputs or tolerance is not a valid repair.

Verification risk: Stage 3 static planning evidence does not prove RTL, simulator, Vivado, or board behavior. Real tool failures must be localized to the earliest causal boundary before any bounded code or contract repair.
Backend/app-shell risk: any later target selection must be derived from cited board materials and real Vivado/tool evidence; ambiguous target names require bounded approval rather than guessing.
output.summary: Proceed from pipeline_planning to parameter_binding. The latest Stage 3 run passed all supplied current-stage checks, command execution succeeded, and SACG memory contains no open retry requests, backtrack requests, or contamination barriers. The next stage must consume only the promoted checker-backed pipeline contract and preserve later-stage obligations for concrete memory/runtime materialization, code generation, hierarchical verification, and backend evidence without treating Stage 3 planning as hardware proof.
